newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Malaysia to invest in Philippine palm oil project.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to invest in Philippine palm oil project.

text.p: Malaysia has forged a joint venture with a Philippine firm to build palm oil mills in southern Philippines, officials from both countries told reporters on Friday.
Malaysia's state of Terengganu plans to invest six billion pesos in the joint venture with Philippine-based Janoub Philippines Development Corp, they said.
The officials did not say how many palm oil mills will be set up by the two parties or the contribution of Janoub Philippines in the project.

The project includes the development of 55,000 hectares of palm farms in the southern Philippine provinces of Lanao del Sur, Tawi-tawi and Maguindanao, said Nur Misuari, governor of the Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (ARMM).
Misuari said palm oil production from the proposed mills will be sold in the domestic market, and the surplus will be exported to other Asian countries, possibly China.

The ARMM covers four semi-autonomous Moslem provinces in the Philippine's Mindanao island headed by Misuari, head of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) which recently signed a peace deal with President Fidel Ramos.

"The launching of this labor-intensive palm oil project (would) help the Mindanao region economically," chief minister Dato Seri Amar di Rajah Tanseri Waw Mokhtar Ahmad of Malaysia's state of Terengganu told reporters.
Road construction and nursery preparation for the palm plantations will start next month, the ARMM said in a separate statement.
Malaysia, one of Asia's largest exporter of vegetable oil, has been investing in palm plantations in other countries in the region.
